close_reason: Renamed jmap-server's opaque pub fn ser to serialize_value. Added a #[deprecated] alias 'ser → serialize_value' that delegates to the new name so existing callers compile-warn rather than break immediately; the alias is documented as scheduled for removal in the next major. Swept all consumer call sites across the workspace: 6 *-server crates' helpers.rs reexports updated to import serialize_value, ~30 source files' use crate::helpers::{... ser ...} imports updated, ~20 ser(x)? call sites and ~15 map(ser).collect sites converted. cargo build/test/clippy/fmt/doc --workspace --all-features all clean.
description:
Path: crate-jmap-server/src/helpers.rs:8. Signature `pub fn ser<T: serde::Serialize>(val: T) -> Result<serde_json::Value, JmapError>`. The function is a thin wrapper around serde_json::to_value that maps the error to JmapError::server_fail.

Verified consumers (rg confirms):
- crate-jmap-chat-server/src/helpers.rs:`pub(crate) use jmap_server::{... ser};`
- crate-jmap-mail-server/src/helpers.rs:`pub(crate) use jmap_server::{... ser};`

Both treat it as part of jmap-server's public API. So changes here ripple.

The name "ser" is opaque. A reader of consumer code seeing `let v = ser(x)?;` cannot tell whether ser is:
- a project-local serializer,
- a re-export from serde,
- a re-export from serde_json,
- this thin JmapError wrapper.

It's also a common short name developers reach for when they need a local serializer ("let ser = ..."), so `use jmap_server::*` could collide invisibly with a consumer's local definition.

Right shape: rename to `serialize_value` or `to_jmap_value`, keep `pub use ser as serialize_value` for one release as a deprecated alias.

Reviewer note: this critique IS about clarity-cost-to-callers, not style for its own sake. The cost shows up the first time a new contributor reads consumer code and has to grep three crates to learn what `ser(x)` does. The fix is one-line; the cost compounds across every consumer for the lifetime of the crate.
title: pub fn ser has opaque 3-letter name in jmap-server's public surface — actively used by every extension server crate
